Roofing in Seabrook, Texas

Seabrook sets its own wind standard, asks for a permit even on roof repairs, and is split by Highway 146 on the state windstorm map. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Seabrook calls.

A bayfront city with its own wind standard

Roofing in Seabrook, TX is shaped by the water. The city sits on Galveston Bay and Clear Lake in Harris County, and it has written its exposure into its building rules: the City of Seabrook says every structure must meet its adopted wind design requirement of 150 mph, measured as an ultimate design wind speed.

Two more things set Seabrook apart. The city's list of work that needs a permit includes roof repairs as well as new roofs, so a patch job here is not automatically permit free the way it can be in some suburbs. And State Highway 146 runs through town as a line on the state windstorm map: the part of Seabrook east of 146 is in the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area, and the part west of it is not.

Houston Expert Roofers does no roofing. Calling the number costs nothing: a recorded assistant takes the call whatever the time, asks what the roof is doing and which part of Seabrook you are in, and connects you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes calls here. That company inspects, quotes and does the work.

East or west of Highway 146

The Texas Department of Insurance describes Seabrook's designated area as the part of the city east of State Highway 146 and inside city limits, and the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association draws the same line for the Harris County cities on its list. Here is what that means for a roof.

Your Seabrook addressState windstorm inspectionWPI-8 certificateTWIA wind and hail coverage
Inside city limits, east of SH 146Yes, during installationIssued by TDI when the work passesPossible; TWIA uses the certificate to decide eligibility
Inside city limits, west of SH 146NoNot issuedNot available, since the address is outside the designated area
Either sideA City of Seabrook permit and the city's 150 mph wind design requirement still apply

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), most roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way (TDI exempts repairs to less than 100 square feet of roof covering that do not touch the decking). When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

In Seabrook, read "Seabrook" in that note as the part of the city east of State Highway 146. If you are unsure which side your lot is on, ask TDI or the city before the contract is signed.

Seabrook permits, step by step

  1. Permit first, for repairs too. The city's permit list includes roof repairs and new roofs, and it says permitted work cannot begin until the Building Department issues the permit.
  2. Watch the fee warning. Seabrook's building permit application says starting work without a permit may lead to the permit fees being doubled. Roof replacement is listed among the residential renovation and repair categories on that form.
  3. Build to 150 mph. Ask the roofer to name the products and fastening it will use to meet the city's adopted wind design requirement, and to put them in the contract.
  4. East of 146, plan the windstorm inspection. The inspection happens while the decking, underlayment and nailing are still visible, so it has to be scheduled during the job, not after.
  5. Keep the file. The permit, the WPI-8 where it applies, the contract and the shingle or panel warranty. Seabrook's public information request log shows owners asking the city for exactly these records when insurers or buyers want them.

The Department of Community Development handles building permits at 1700 First Street, and its office number is 281-291-5669. Rules and fees change, so confirm the current process with the city.

After a storm: Ike, Harvey and Beryl in Seabrook

Seabrook knows what a direct hit looks like. When Hurricane Ike came ashore at Galveston in September 2008, the Harris County Flood Control District recorded storm surge of 12 to 15 feet across Harris County. A Houston Chronicle retrospective reported that 76 percent of Seabrook's residential properties were damaged, and that some waterfront homes on Todville Road were ripped apart or washed away.

When Hurricane Harvey damaged homes in 2017, the City of Seabrook set up a Storm Damage Recovery Permit. Its written procedure let owners list the repair work with approximate costs, and allowed them to keep removing damaged material from the home before applying for or receiving that permit. Whether the city opens a similar process after a future storm is its decision, so watch the city's announcements.

Seabrook roofs have had more recent tests. Hurricane Beryl came ashore near Matagorda on July 8, 2024 and, according to Community Impact's Bay Area edition, left over 2.2 million CenterPoint Energy customers without power across the region. Wind off open water drives rain sideways under shingle edges and around flashing, so a roof that came through with no visible damage can still have a weak spot. After Beryl the city also posted an online Storm Damage Report form for residents. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Why Seabrook homeowners call the line

A roofer that knows the 146 line

Whether your job needs a WPI-8 depends on which side of State Highway 146 you live on. When you are put through, say where you are and ask how the company handles windstorm inspections there.

Small repairs still need paperwork

Because Seabrook permits roof repairs, a quick patch by someone passing through can leave you out of step with the city. A local roofing company should pull the permit as a matter of course.

Metal and shingle questions

Waterfront homes weigh metal panels against shingles for wind and salt air. The company you reach can explain what meets the city's wind requirement on your house and what each choice costs.

Nights, weekends and holidays included, a call costs you nothing. The roofing company quotes and bills you directly, and companies may pay the line a referral fee.

Questions to ask a Seabrook roofer

  • Is my address east or west of State Highway 146, and does this job need the state windstorm inspection?
  • Which products and fastening will you use to meet Seabrook's 150 mph wind design requirement?
  • Will you pull the city permit before any work, including a repair?
  • How will you protect flashing, fasteners and metal edges from salt air?
  • Can you send your certificate of liability insurance and the WPI-8 from a recent job, with the owner's details removed?
  • What does your workmanship warranty cover, for how long, in writing?

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Not sure whether your side of Seabrook needs the windstorm inspection, or whether the damage is a repair or a new roof? Call and describe it. The roofing company you are connected with looks in person and writes its own estimate.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Does roofing repair in Seabrook need a permit?

Yes, in most cases. The City of Seabrook's list of work that needs a permit includes new roofs and roof repairs, and the city says work that needs a permit cannot start until the Building Department issues it. Its permit application warns that starting without a permit may lead to doubled permit fees. Ask the roofer to file before any work begins. The city's Community Development office is at 281-291-5669. See the roof repair page for what a sound repair includes.

Is all of Seabrook in the windstorm catastrophe area?

No. The Texas Department of Insurance and the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association describe Seabrook's designated area as the part inside city limits and east of State Highway 146. East of 146, roof work goes through the state windstorm inspection and earns a WPI-8. West of 146 it does not. Check where your address sits before you sign a contract.

What wind speed does a new roof in Seabrook have to meet?

The City of Seabrook says all structures must meet its adopted wind design requirement of 150 mph, stated as an ultimate design wind speed. For new construction the city wants plans sealed by a Texas structural engineer who is on the TDI list for high wind zones. For a re-roof, ask the roofer which shingle or metal panel, underlayment and fastening it will use to meet the city's standard.

How can I find out if a Seabrook house has roof permits or a windstorm certificate?

Ask the city. Seabrook's public information request log shows residents asking for roof permit history and windstorm certifications on specific properties, often for insurance. If you are buying a home east of Highway 146, ask the seller for the WPI-8 too. A missing certificate is worth sorting out before closing, not after.

Who handles my roof if I call about roofing in Seabrook?

An independent, locally owned roofing company that takes calls in Seabrook. Houston Expert Roofers only answers the phone: an automated assistant asks about the roof and where you live, then transfers you. After that, the roofing company inspects, writes a quote and handles the job, collecting payment from you itself. The call is free, and companies may pay the line a referral fee.
